API Reference

Complete reference for the public functions in cube_explorer.api, the GUI-free interface for scripts and notebooks.

Every entry on this page is generated from the function’s own docstring, so it always matches the code. For task-oriented walkthroughs, see the User Guide.

from cube_explorer.api import load_cube, fit_line

Note

cube.wavelength is an astropy Quantity, so it carries its unit. Use cube.wavelength.value when a function or comparison needs plain numbers.

Note

The map functions (the Gaussian map, the Flux Map, the continuum cubes, and the rotational diagram maps) use several processes. On Windows and macOS, put the code of your script under if __name__ == "__main__":.

Data Loading

cube_explorer.api.load_cube(filename)[source]

Load a FITS data cube from file.

This function handles multi-instrument FITS files (MUSE, MIRI, NIRSpec) with automatic instrument detection.

Parameters:

filename (str) – Path to FITS file

Returns:

Object containing cube data, wavelength, WCS, and metadata

Return type:

CubeData

Raises:

ValueError – If instrument cannot be detected or file is invalid

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("Level3_ch1-long_s3d.fits")
>>> print(cube.instrument)  # "MIRI"
>>> print(cube.wavelength.shape)  # (1000,)
>>> print(cube.cube.shape)  # (1000, 512, 512)
cube_explorer.api.load_spectrum(filename, x_column=None, y_column=None, error_column=None, wave_unit=None, flux_unit=None, medium=None, instrument=None, grating=None)[source]

Load one spectrum from a text file (txt or csv) or a 1D FITS table, for example a JWST x1d file. This is the same as the GUI’s “Load Spectrum” button.

The file has a wavelength column, a flux column and an optional flux error column. The separator can be a tab, a comma, a semicolon or white space. Lines that start with “#” are comments. A file that “Save Spectrum” wrote gives its own units, instrument and column names. Any other text file needs wave_unit. A FITS table gives the unit of each column. For an x1d file the flux is FLUX in Jy, unless y_column is SURF_BRIGHT (MJy/sr). The error column and the flux unit then follow the flux column. The object has no cube. cube.spectrum, cube.wavelength, cube.header and cube.spectrum_error work as they do for a cube, so fit_continuum and fit_line take them in the same way.

Parameters:

  • filename (str) – Path to the text file or the FITS file

  • x_column (str or int) – Name or index of the wavelength column. None uses the guess from the column names.

  • y_column (str or int) – Name or index of the flux column. None uses the guess.

  • error_column (str, int or False) – Name or index of the flux error column. None uses the guess. False means that no column is the error.

  • wave_unit (str) – ‘um’, ‘nm’ or ‘Angstrom’. Needed if the file does not give it. nm is converted to um.

  • flux_unit (str) – Flux unit, for example ‘Jy’. None uses the file’s unit, or leaves it unknown.

  • medium (str) – ‘air’ or ‘vacuum’. None uses the file’s value, or leaves it unknown.

  • instrument (str) – ‘MIRI’, ‘NIRSpec’ or ‘MUSE’. It gives the resolving power for the multi-Gaussian fit.

  • grating (str) – NIRSpec grating, for example ‘G395H’. Needed for the resolving power of NIRSpec.

Returns:

Object with spectrum, wavelength, wave_unit, flux_unit, header and spectrum_error. cube is None.

Return type:

CubeData

Raises:

  • ValueError – If a column or unit is not valid, wave_unit is missing, or fewer than 10 usable rows are left

  • OSError – If the file cannot be opened

Example

>>> spec = load_spectrum("my_spectrum.csv", wave_unit="um", flux_unit="Jy")
>>> result = fit_line(spec.wavelength, spec.spectrum, x1=6.90, x2=6.92)
cube_explorer.api.load_fit(filename, wavelength=None, spectrum=None)[source]

Load a Gaussian fit file that “Save Fit” (or the save_path of fit_line and fit_hitran_lines) wrote. It gives the fit back as it was, with no new fit. This is the same as the GUI’s “Load Fit” (single line) and “Load Fits” (multi-Gaussian) buttons.

Parameters:

  • filename (str) – Path to the fit file

  • wavelength (array-like) – Wavelengths of the spectrum that the fit goes on. None uses the wavelengths in the file. Given wavelengths must be the wavelengths of the file.

  • spectrum (array-like or Quantity) – Flux of the spectrum. None uses the flux in the file. A Quantity gives its unit, which must be the unit of the file.

Returns:

‘fit_type’ (‘single’ or ‘multi’), ‘lines’ (list of dicts with ‘kind’ (‘line’, ‘contaminant’ or

’skipped’), ‘line’ (catalog data) and ‘result’ (GaussianFitResult), in the order of the file), ‘markers’ (the fit markers of a single fit), ‘tab’, ‘wave_unit’, ‘flux_unit’, ‘baseline_source’, ‘wavelength’, ‘spectrum’, ‘fit’ and ‘baseline’ (arrays), and ‘notes’ (warnings, may be empty).

Return type:

dict

Raises:

  • ValueError – If the file has no fit parameters (a file from an older version), the wavelengths are not the wavelengths of the file (a Doppler shift gives this error), or the flux unit of the spectrum is not the flux unit of the file.

  • OSError – If the file cannot be opened

Example

>>> fit = load_fit("gaussian_fit.txt")
>>> print(fit['lines'][0]['result'].center)

Region Extraction

cube_explorer.api.extract_pixel_spectrum(cube, x, y)[source]

Extract the 1D spectrum at a single spatial pixel. This is the same lookup the GUI uses; prefer it over indexing cube.cube directly, since it always applies the correct (wavelength, y, x) axis order.

Parameters:

  • cube (CubeData) – Loaded cube, as returned by load_cube()

  • x (int) – X pixel coordinate (0-based)

  • y (int) – Y pixel coordinate (0-based)

Returns:

1D spectrum at (x, y), same length as cube.wavelength. It is the flux of that pixel in Jy for a cube in MJy/sr (the cube value times the pixel solid angle), the same as the GUI shows, and the unit goes with the data.

Return type:

astropy.units.Quantity

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> spectrum = extract_pixel_spectrum(cube, x=20, y=25)
cube_explorer.api.extract_region_spectrum(cube, mask)[source]

Extract the summed spectrum over an arbitrary spatial region, the same sum the GUI shows for region selections (each reduces to a 2D boolean mask). A NaN pixel adds 0 to the sum instead of giving NaN.

Parameters:

  • cube (CubeData) – Loaded cube, as returned by load_cube()

  • mask (numpy.ndarray) – 2D boolean array matching the cube’s spatial shape (cube.cube.shape[1:]); True marks pixels inside the region

Returns:

1D summed spectrum of the masked pixels. It is a flux in Jy for a cube in MJy/sr (the sum times the pixel solid angle), the same as the GUI shows, and the unit goes with the data.

Return type:

astropy.units.Quantity

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> mask = np.zeros(cube.cube.shape[1:], dtype=bool)
>>> mask[15:35, 10:30] = True  # a rectangular region, [y, x] order
>>> spectrum = extract_region_spectrum(cube, mask)

Regions

cube_explorer.api.make_region_mask(shape, coords, target_shape, verts=None)[source]

Make a boolean mask of a region from its shape and its pixel coordinates. The mask has True for the pixels that the region touches, the same as a region that you draw in the GUI. Use it as mask in extract_region_spectrum or fit_region.

Parameters:

  • shape (str) – ‘POINT’, ‘RECTANGLE’, ‘CIRCLE’, ‘ELLIPSE’ or ‘POLYGON’

  • coords (tuple) – (x, y) for ‘POINT’. (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) in pixels for ‘RECTANGLE’, ‘CIRCLE’ and ‘ELLIPSE’. The circle and the ellipse fill that box. Not used for ‘POLYGON’.

  • target_shape (tuple) – (height, width) of the image, for example cube.cube.shape[1:]

  • verts (array-like, optional) – (N, 2) polygon vertices as (x, y) pixels. Needed for ‘POLYGON’.

Returns:

2D boolean array of shape target_shape

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

Raises:

ValueError – if the shape is not known, or a polygon has no vertices

Example

>>> mask = make_region_mask('CIRCLE', (20, 30, 15, 25), cube.cube.shape[1:])
>>> spectrum = extract_region_spectrum(cube, mask)
cube_explorer.api.save_region(path, shape, coords, cube_data, verts=None, source_desc=None)[source]

Save a region to a text file, as RA and Dec sky coordinates. This is Save Region in the GUI. The file works on any image of the same field. Read it with load_region.

Parameters:

  • path (str) – Path of the text file to write

  • shape (str) – ‘POINT’, ‘RECTANGLE’, ‘CIRCLE’, ‘ELLIPSE’ or ‘POLYGON’

  • coords (tuple) – Pixel coordinates, see make_region_mask

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube. Its WCS turns the pixels into sky coordinates.

  • verts (array-like, optional) – (N, 2) polygon vertices as (x, y) pixels. Needed for ‘POLYGON’.

  • source_desc (str, optional) – Note for the header of the file. None uses the name of the cube file.

Returns:

None

Raises:

ValueError – if the shape is not known, a polygon has no vertices, or the cube has no celestial WCS

cube_explorer.api.load_region(path, cube_data)[source]

Read a region file and turn it into a boolean mask on the pixel grid of a cube. This is Import Region in the GUI. The file can come from another image of the same field, because it holds sky coordinates.

Parameters:

  • path (str) – Path of a region file that Save Region wrote

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube that the mask is for

Returns:

2D boolean array, shape (ny, nx) of the cube. Use it as mask in extract_region_spectrum or fit_region, or in region_masks.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

Raises:

ValueError – if the file is not a region file, the cube has no celestial WCS, or the region is outside the cube

Example

>>> mask = load_region("my_region.txt", cube)
>>> spectrum = extract_region_spectrum(cube, mask)

Gaussian Line Fitting

cube_explorer.api.fit_line(wavelength, spectrum, x1, x2, line_name=None, peak_x=None, header=None, wave_unit=None, save_path=None, parameters_path=None, continuum=None)[source]

Fit a Gaussian to an emission line in a spectrum. The fitter needs a starting guess for the line center; here it defaults to the brightest sample between x1 and x2, or pass peak_x explicitly.

Parameters:

  • wavelength (array-like) – Wavelength/frequency values. Astropy Quantities are accepted; their units are stripped.

  • spectrum (array-like or Quantity) – Flux values. A Quantity (like cube.spectrum, which is in Jy for a cube in MJy/sr) gives its own unit, and that unit is used instead of the BUNIT of header.

  • x1 (float) – Left boundary of the fitting region.

  • x2 (float) – Right boundary of the fitting region.

  • line_name (str, optional) – Descriptive label for the line. Not stored on the result; it exists for readability at the call site.

  • peak_x (float, optional) – Initial guess for the line center. Defaults to the brightest wavelength between x1 and x2.

  • header (optional) – FITS header used for unit conversion. Pass cube.header to match what the GUI produces.

  • wave_unit (str, optional) – Spectral axis unit, e.g. cube.wave_unit.

  • save_path (str, optional) – If given, write a tab-separated text file with the columns wavelength, original spectrum, fit and original minus fit (the GUI’s “Save Fit” file). The fit is NaN outside x1 to x2. Nothing is written, and a warning is raised, if the fit failed.

  • parameters_path (str, optional) – If given, write a tab-separated text file with the fitted parameters (the GUI’s “Save Parameters” file). The same rule applies if the fit failed.

  • continuum (array-like, optional) – Pre-fitted continuum, same length as wavelength. When given, it is the baseline of the fit, as in the GUI when a continuum is fitted for the spectrum. If None (default), the baseline is the straight line between the flux values at x1 and x2. The fit fails if the continuum has no value where the flux has data.

Returns:

Object with amplitude, center, sigma, fwhm, area, area_unit, area_native, baseline_slope, baseline_intercept, r_squared, success and message.

area is in erg/s/cm^2 when the spectrum is in Jy (header is not needed), or when it is in MJy/sr and header is supplied (MIRI, NIRSpec); otherwise it stays in flux*wavelength units. Check area_unit rather than assuming; it always states which. area_native is the unconverted value, which is what you want when dividing by a continuum measured in the cube’s own units.

Return type:

GaussianFitResult

Raises:

ValueError – If no wavelength samples lie between x1 and x2, or if every flux value in that window is NaN.

Example

>>> result = fit_line(
...     wavelength=cube.wavelength,
...     spectrum=cube.spectrum,
...     x1=6.90,
...     x2=6.95,
...     line_name="H2 S(5)"
... )
>>> if result.success:
...     print(f"Line center: {result.center} um")
...     print(f"FWHM: {result.fwhm:.6f} um")

Full-Cube Fitting

cube_explorer.api.create_gaussian_map(cube_data, lam_min=None, lam_max=None, n_jobs=None, **kwargs)[source]

Fit a Gaussian to every spatial pixel’s spectrum in a wavelength window.

This is the same full-cube fitting used by the GUI’s Gaussian mapping dialog. Iterative sigma-clipping outlier rejection is always enabled.

Parameters:

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube from load_cube()

  • lam_min (float, optional) – Minimum wavelength for the fit window (default: full range)

  • lam_max (float, optional) – Maximum wavelength for the fit window (default: full range)

  • n_jobs (int, optional) – Number of worker processes (default: auto-detect CPUs)

  • **kwargs – Passed through to fit_gaussians_per_pixel (e.g. fac_above_stdres, noise_min, noise_max, lambda_0, progress_callback)

Returns:

2D parameter maps - ‘amplitude’, ‘continuum’, ‘center’, ‘sigma’, ‘fwhm’, ‘area’,

’r_squared’, ‘success’, ‘is_detection’, ‘is_upper_limit’. ‘continuum’ is the baseline of each pixel at ‘continuum_wavelength’, in the flux unit of the cube

Return type:

dict

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> maps = create_gaussian_map(cube, lam_min=4.65, lam_max=4.70)
>>> print(f"Detections: {maps['is_detection'].sum()}")
cube_explorer.api.create_velocity_map(cube_data, maps, rest_wavelength, systemic_velocity=0.0)[source]

Make a Doppler velocity map from Gaussian map line centers and a rest wavelength. Zero velocity is the rest wavelength, in um (vacuum), as find_rest_lines() gives it. The function converts it to the air or vacuum wavelengths that the cube uses.

Parameters:

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube from load_cube()

  • maps (dict) – Result of create_gaussian_map()

  • rest_wavelength (float) – Rest wavelength of the line, in um (vacuum)

  • systemic_velocity (float, optional) – Systemic velocity in km/s. The map is relative to it. This is the “Systemic velocity” box of the Velocity map in the GUI. Only this map changes.

Returns:

Velocity map in km/s. A pixel without a fitted center is NaN.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

Raises:

ValueError – if the cube header does not say if wavelengths are in air or in vacuum, the spectral axis is not a wavelength, or systemic_velocity is not a finite number greater than -c

cube_explorer.api.find_rest_lines(molecule, lam_min, lam_max, line_list_path=None)[source]

List the lines of one molecule that can set zero velocity, in a wavelength window. It reads HITRAN and the LST catalog, and every line stays in the list. Pass the ‘wavelength’ of the line you pick to create_velocity_map().

Parameters:

  • molecule (str) – Molecule or atom name, for example ‘CO’, ‘H2’ or ‘He I’

  • lam_min (float) – Lower end of the window, in um (vacuum)

  • lam_max (float) – Upper end of the window, in um (vacuum)

  • line_list_path (str, optional) – CSV file, HITRAN-format .par file (for example HITEMP), or LST .lst file with more lines of this molecule. Its lines have a ‘source’ that starts with ‘File’.

Returns:

Line dicts sorted by wavelength. ‘wavelength’ is in um (vacuum), and ‘source’

is ‘HITRAN’, ‘LST’ or ‘File: <name>’.

Return type:

list

Raises:

ValueError – if the window is not 0 < lam_min < lam_max, or line_list_path is not a readable line list of this molecule

cube_explorer.api.export_residual_cube(cube_data, maps, out_path='residual_cube.fits')[source]

Save the residual cube of a Gaussian map to a FITS file. This is the “Residuals” export of the Gaussian map window. The residuals are the ones that the map kept when it fitted each pixel: (data - fit) / noise, inside the fit window. Nothing is fitted again.

Parameters:

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube that the map was fitted on. It gives the header.

  • maps (dict) – Result of create_gaussian_map(). It must have ‘residuals_cube’.

  • out_path (str) – Output FITS filename (default “residual_cube.fits”)

Returns:

The FITS file is written to out_path. To use the residuals as an array, read maps[‘residuals_cube’].

Return type:

None

Raises:

ValueError – if maps has no ‘residuals_cube’, for example a map that was cancelled

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> maps = create_gaussian_map(cube, lam_min=4.65, lam_max=4.70)
>>> export_residual_cube(cube, maps, out_path="residual.fits")
cube_explorer.api.save_gaussian_map(cube_data, maps, parameter, out_path, lam_min, lam_max, peak_wavelength=None, rest_wavelength=None, rest_label=None, systemic_velocity=0.0, species=None)[source]

Save one parameter of a Gaussian map to a FITS file. This is the Export button of the Gaussian map window. The header has the fit window, the unit and the keywords that the parameter needs (for example VSYS for the Velocity map and CONTWAV for the Continuum map).

Parameters:

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube that the map was fitted on

  • maps (dict) – Result of create_gaussian_map()

  • parameter (str) – One of ‘area’, ‘area_error’, ‘amplitude’, ‘continuum’, ‘center’, ‘velocity’, ‘sigma’, ‘fwhm’, ‘chi2’, ‘fit_status’, ‘success_mask’

  • out_path (str) – Path of the FITS file to write

  • lam_min (float) – Start of the fit window, in the wavelength unit of the cube

  • lam_max (float) – End of the fit window, in the wavelength unit of the cube

  • peak_wavelength (float, optional) – Wavelength of the line peak. None uses the middle of the window.

  • rest_wavelength (float, optional) – Rest wavelength in um (vacuum). The Velocity map needs it.

  • rest_label (str, optional) – Short text that names the rest line, for the header

  • systemic_velocity (float) – Systemic velocity in km/s that the Velocity map is relative to

  • species (str, optional) – Species of the line, for example ‘H2’. For the Area map only. It adds the HITRAN constants of the nearest line, so import_line_map can read the file.

Returns:

None

Raises:

ValueError – if the parameter is not known, or the Velocity map has no rest_wavelength

Example

>>> maps = create_gaussian_map(cube, lam_min=17.02, lam_max=17.05, lambda_0=17.0348)
>>> save_gaussian_map(cube, maps, 'area', 's1_area.fits', 17.02, 17.05,
...                   peak_wavelength=17.0348, species='H2')
cube_explorer.api.save_gaussian_maps(cube_data, maps, out_dir, lam_min, lam_max, parameters=None, peak_wavelength=None, rest_wavelength=None, rest_label=None, systemic_velocity=0.0, species=None, base_name=None)[source]

Save several parameters of a Gaussian map, one FITS file for each, in one folder. The names are <cube name>_gaussian_<parameter>.fits. The Velocity map is left out when there is no rest_wavelength.

Parameters:

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube that the map was fitted on

  • maps (dict) – Result of create_gaussian_map()

  • out_dir (str) – Folder for the files. It is made if it does not exist.

  • lam_min (float) – Start of the fit window, in the wavelength unit of the cube

  • lam_max (float) – End of the fit window, in the wavelength unit of the cube

  • parameters (list, optional) – Parameter names, see save_gaussian_map. None writes all of them.

  • peak_wavelength – See save_gaussian_map

  • rest_wavelength – See save_gaussian_map

  • rest_label – See save_gaussian_map

  • systemic_velocity – See save_gaussian_map

  • species – See save_gaussian_map

  • base_name (str, optional) – First part of each file name. None uses the name of the cube file.

Returns:

The paths of the files that were written

Return type:

list

Continuum Fitting

cube_explorer.api.fit_continuum(wavelength, flux, method='auto', **kwargs)[source]

Fit continuum to a spectrum using automatic peak detection: the same method the GUI uses, detecting emission/absorption peaks and fitting a smooth continuum through the remaining points.

Parameters:

  • wavelength (array-like) – Wavelength/frequency values

  • flux (array-like) – Flux values

  • method (str) – Fitting method - currently only ‘auto’ is supported

Keyword Arguments:

  • window_size (int) – Size of median filter window (default 51, must be odd)

  • sigma_threshold (float) – Prominence threshold in sigma (default 2.0)

  • peak_width (int) – Minimum width of peaks in pixels (default 1)

  • peak_distance (int) – Minimum distance between peaks (default 3)

  • peak_exclusion (int) – Pixels to exclude on each side of peak (default 3)

  • iterations (int) – Iterative clipping iterations (default 2)

  • smoothing_factor (float) – Spline smoothing divisor (default 5). A higher value follows the data more closely. The smoothing follows the noise of the spectrum, so it does not depend on the flux unit.

  • mask_ranges (list) – (low, high) wavelength pairs, in the unit of wavelength (default None). The points in these ranges are not used to fit the continuum. The continuum crosses a masked range as a smooth curve between its two sides. The same key works in the continuum_params of save_continuum_cubes, extract_flux and create_flux_map.

Returns:

Fitted continuum values matching input wavelength array. If flux is an astropy Quantity (like cube.spectrum, which is in Jy), the continuum has the same unit, so spectrum - continuum works. A plain array in gives a plain array out.

Return type:

array or Quantity

Raises:

ValueError – if a masked range is not valid, or if fewer than 10 points are outside the masked ranges

Example

>>> wavelength = cube.wavelength
>>> spectrum = cube.spectrum
>>> continuum = fit_continuum(wavelength, spectrum, sigma_threshold=2.0)
>>> line_only = spectrum - continuum
cube_explorer.api.measure_equivalent_width(fit_result, wavelength=None, continuum_spectrum=None)[source]

Calculate equivalent width (the width of an imaginary rectangular line with the same area) from a Gaussian fit result. A full continuum array is averaged over the wavelengths actually fitted.

Parameters:

  • fit_result (GaussianFitResult) – Result from fit_line().

  • wavelength (array-like, optional) – Wavelength array matching continuum_spectrum. Required when passing a continuum array.

  • continuum_spectrum (array-like or float, optional) – Continuum-only spectrum, or a single continuum level. If omitted, the fit’s own baseline is used.

Returns:

Equivalent width in the same units as wavelength. Returns 0.0 if the fit failed or the continuum level is non-positive.

Return type:

float

Raises:

ValueError – If a continuum array is given without a wavelength array.

Example

>>> continuum = fit_continuum(cube.wavelength, cube.spectrum)
>>> ew = measure_equivalent_width(result, cube.wavelength, continuum)
>>> print(f"Equivalent width: {ew:.6f} um")
cube_explorer.api.save_continuum_masks(filename, mask_ranges, wave_unit=None, shift_factor=1.0)[source]

Save masked wavelength ranges of the automatic continuum to a tab-separated text file. This is the same file as the GUI’s Save Masks button writes. The file gives the wavelength unit and the Doppler shift factor, so load_continuum_masks can put the ranges on the right axis.

Parameters:

  • filename (str) – Path of the text file to write

  • mask_ranges (list) – (low, high) wavelength pairs, in wave_unit

  • wave_unit (str, optional) – Wavelength unit of the pairs, for example ‘um’ or ‘Angstrom’. None writes “Unknown”, and a load then cannot convert units.

  • shift_factor (float, optional) – Doppler shift factor of the wavelength axis. It is 1.0 if the axis is not shifted. A Doppler shift of v km/s in the GUI gives a factor of 1 / (1 + v/c).

Returns:

None

Raises:

  • ValueError – if a masked range is not valid

  • OSError – if the file cannot be written

Example

>>> save_continuum_masks("masks.txt", [(6.90, 6.93), (7.10, 7.15)], wave_unit="um")
cube_explorer.api.load_continuum_masks(filename, wave_unit=None, shift_factor=1.0)[source]

Load masked wavelength ranges from a text file that save_continuum_masks or the GUI wrote. The ranges are moved onto the axis you give. If the file was saved in another unit, or with another Doppler shift, the ranges stay on the same part of the spectrum.

Parameters:

  • filename (str) – Path of the masks file

  • wave_unit (str, optional) – Wavelength unit of the spectrum that you use the ranges on, for example ‘um’. None keeps the unit of the file.

  • shift_factor (float, optional) – Doppler shift factor of the wavelength axis of that spectrum. It is 1.0 if the axis is not shifted. A file that gives no shift factor is not moved.

Returns:

Sorted (low, high) tuples of float on your axis, ready for mask_ranges in fit_continuum.

Return type:

list

Raises:

  • OSError – if the file cannot be opened

  • ValueError – if the file has no range or a bad line, or if its unit is not the same kind of unit as wave_unit

Example

>>> masks = load_continuum_masks("masks.txt", wave_unit="um")
>>> continuum = fit_continuum(cube.wavelength, cube.spectrum, mask_ranges=masks)
cube_explorer.api.save_continuum_cubes(cube_data, continuum_path, contsub_path, continuum_params=None, anchor_wavelengths=None, n_jobs=None)[source]

Fit the continuum at every pixel, then save two cubes: the continuum and the continuum-subtracted (line-only) cube. The same as the GUI’s Save Continuum Cubes button. The two cubes always sum to the original.

Two methods: automatic (the default), or anchor_wavelengths, the same wavelengths you would click in the GUI’s Custom Continuum tool. With anchors, each pixel gets a cubic spline through its own flux at the anchors (median of +/- 7 instrumental sigma, clipped at 3 sigma), held flat beyond the first and last anchor. Scripts that call this need an if __name__ == "__main__": guard on Windows/macOS.

Parameters:

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube from load_cube()

  • continuum_path (str) – Output FITS path of the continuum cube

  • contsub_path (str) – Output FITS path of the continuum-subtracted cube

  • continuum_params (dict, optional) – Override the fit_continuum() keyword arguments (window_size, sigma_threshold, peak_width, peak_distance, peak_exclusion, iterations, smoothing_factor). The same values apply to every pixel. If None, uses the defaults. Not allowed together with anchor_wavelengths.

  • anchor_wavelengths (array-like, optional) – At least 3 wavelengths, in the units of cube_data.wavelength. If given, uses the anchor method instead of the automatic one.

  • n_jobs (int, optional) – Number of worker processes (default: auto-detect CPUs, capped by available memory)

Returns:

Number of pixels that have data but got no continuum (automatic: too

few valid points; anchors: fewer than 3 valid anchors). They are NaN in both cubes.

Return type:

int

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> n_failed = save_continuum_cubes(cube, "cube_continuum.fits", "cube_contsub.fits")
>>> n_failed = save_continuum_cubes(
...     cube, "cube_continuum.fits", "cube_contsub.fits",
...     anchor_wavelengths=[6.55, 6.70, 6.95, 7.20, 7.35])

Flux Analysis

cube_explorer.api.fit_hitran_lines(wavelength, spectrum, molecule, wavelength_min=None, wavelength_max=None, isotopologue=1, refresh_cache=False, v_upper=None, v_lower=None, header=None, wave_unit=None, continuum=None, contam_catalog=None, save_path=None, parameters_path=None)[source]

Fit HITRAN spectral lines automatically using database lookup. Same algorithm as the GUI’s Multi-Gaussian Fit: every requested line and any contaminant sharing its chunk fit simultaneously, so they don’t double-claim flux.

Parameters:

  • wavelength (array-like) – Wavelength/frequency values

  • spectrum (array-like) – Flux values

  • molecule (str) – Molecule name (e.g., ‘CO’, ‘H2O’, ‘CH4’, ‘[Fe II]’)

  • wavelength_min (float, optional) – Minimum wavelength to search. If None, uses spectrum min.

  • wavelength_max (float, optional) – Maximum wavelength to search. If None, uses spectrum max.

  • isotopologue (int) – Isotopologue number (default 1 for main isotope)

  • refresh_cache (bool) – Force refresh HITRAN cache (default False)

  • v_upper (int, optional) – Filter by upper vibrational level (e.g., 1 for v=1)

  • v_lower (int, optional) – Filter by lower vibrational level (e.g., 0 for v=0)

  • header – FITS header. Required whenever any line is actually found – each line’s fit width comes from the instrument’s real spectral resolution at that wavelength (MIRI/NIRSpec only), not a guess, so a missing header raises ValueError rather than silently fitting with the wrong width. Also used for the erg/s/cm2 conversion.

  • wave_unit – Wavelength unit string, needed alongside header for the conversion.

  • continuum (array-like, optional) – Pre-fitted continuum, same length as wavelength, subtracted before fitting each line. If None, one is fitted automatically via fit_continuum() – the same fallback the GUI uses when you have not run Automatic Continuum interactively first.

  • contam_catalog (pd.DataFrame, optional) – Non-target lines (a ‘line_wave_um’ column, same format as load_contaminating_lines_catalog()) to give their own component in the fit so they don’t distort a nearby requested line’s amplitude – the same optional catalog extract_flux/Flux Map already supports. None (default) skips this.

  • save_path (str, optional) – If given, write a tab-separated text file with the columns wavelength, original spectrum, fit and original minus fit (the GUI’s “Save Fit” file). The fit includes the contaminant lines and is NaN where no line was fitted. Nothing is written, and a warning is raised, if no line fit succeeded.

  • parameters_path (str, optional) – If given, write a tab-separated text file with one row for each line: the fitted parameters, the catalog data, and a flag for an unreliable area error (the GUI’s “Save Parameters” file). Lines that could not be fit are listed as skipped with the reason. The same rule applies if no line fit succeeded.

Returns:

List of dicts with fit results for each line:

  • wavelength: Fitted line center wavelength

  • species: Molecule name

  • transition: Transition description

  • amplitude: Peak height above the local continuum

  • sigma: Gaussian sigma width

  • fwhm: Full width at half maximum

  • area: Integrated line flux, in the units given by area_unit

  • area_native: Integrated line flux before any CGS conversion

  • area_unit: Units of area – 'erg/s/cm^2' only when header/wave_unit let it convert; always check this rather than assuming

  • r_squared: Fit quality

  • success: Whether fit succeeded

  • message: Status message

Return type:

list

Raises:

RuntimeError – if the HITRAN fetch fails, or HITRAN does not know the molecule

Example

>>> # Fit CO v=1->0 lines only
>>> results = fit_hitran_lines(
...     wavelength=cube.wavelength,
...     spectrum=spectrum,
...     molecule='CO',
...     wavelength_min=4.7,
...     wavelength_max=4.8,
...     v_upper=1,
...     v_lower=0,
...     header=cube.header,
...     wave_unit=cube.wave_unit,
... )
>>> detected = [r for r in results if r['success']]
>>> print(f"Detected {len(detected)} CO v=1->0 lines")
cube_explorer.api.extract_flux(wavelength, spectrum, target_catalog_path, contamination_catalog_path=None, continuum_params=None, header=None, wave_unit=None)[source]

Extract total flux by fitting all target lines in a spectrum simultaneously with contaminating lines and continuum; the same algorithm as the GUI’s Flux Map button, run on a single spectrum.

Parameters:

  • wavelength (array-like) – Wavelength values in same units as catalog

  • spectrum (array-like) – Flux values

  • target_catalog_path (str) – Path to target line catalog (ECSV format)

  • contamination_catalog_path (str, optional) – Path to contaminant lines catalog

  • continuum_params (dict, optional) – Override the default continuum-fitting parameters (window_size, sigma_threshold, peak_width, peak_distance, peak_exclusion, iterations, smoothing_factor). If None, uses the defaults, which work well for typical spectra.

  • header – FITS header. Required whenever any line is actually detected – each line’s fit width comes from the instrument’s real spectral resolution at that wavelength (MIRI/NIRSpec only), not a guess, so a missing header raises ValueError as soon as a line is found rather than silently fitting with the wrong width. Also used to convert ‘flux’/’contam_flux’ to erg/s/cm2 – ‘flux_unit’ in the result always tells you which you got.

  • wave_unit (str, optional) – Wavelength unit (e.g. ‘um’). Used alongside header for the CGS conversion.

Returns:

Results containing:

  • ’flux’: Total flux, in erg/s/cm2 if header/wave_unit were given and the conversion is supported for this instrument, else native units

  • ’contam_flux’: Total flux attributed to contaminating lines, same units

  • ’flux_unit’: unit of ‘flux’/’contam_flux’

  • ’mean_continuum’: Mean continuum level used for the fit (native units)

  • ’detected_lines’: DataFrame of individual detected line fits

  • ’residuals’: DataFrame of fit residuals

  • ’continuum_curve’: DataFrame of the fitted continuum vs wavelength

Return type:

dict

Example

>>> result = extract_flux(
...     wavelength=cube.wavelength,
...     spectrum=cube.spectrum,
...     target_catalog_path="CO/CO_comprehensive_linelist_with_g.ecsv",
...     header=cube.header,
...     wave_unit=cube.wave_unit,
... )
>>> print(f"Total flux: {result['flux']:.4e} {result['flux_unit']}")
>>> print(f"Detected {len(result['detected_lines'])} lines")
cube_explorer.api.create_flux_map(cube_data, target_catalog_path=None, contamination_catalog_path=None, n_jobs=8, wavelength_min=None, wavelength_max=None, continuum_params=None)[source]

Create a 2D map of target-line flux across the entire data cube: HITRAN CO by default, or a custom target_catalog_path. Same algorithm as the GUI’s Flux Map button (continuum subtraction, then per-pixel fit).

Parameters:

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube from load_cube()

  • target_catalog_path (str, optional) – Path to target line catalog (ECSV format). If None, automatically fetches CO from HITRAN.

  • contamination_catalog_path (str, optional) – Path to contaminant lines

  • n_jobs (int) – Number of parallel jobs (default 8)

  • wavelength_min (float, optional) – Min wavelength to fit, and for the HITRAN search when target_catalog_path is None (auto-detect if None)

  • wavelength_max (float, optional) – Max wavelength to fit, and for the HITRAN search when target_catalog_path is None (auto-detect if None)

  • continuum_params (dict, optional) – Override the default continuum-fitting parameters, applied identically to every pixel. If None, uses the defaults, which work well for typical spectra.

Returns:

Map data containing:

  • ’flux_map’: 2D array of flux per pixel, in erg/s/cm2 if cube_data.header supports the conversion (see ‘flux_unit’), else the cube’s native flux unit. A pixel with no detected line is NaN

  • ’contam_flux_map’: 2D array of contaminating-line flux per pixel, same units as ‘flux_map’. A pixel with no detected contaminating line is NaN

  • ’detection_map’: 2D array with number of detected target lines per pixel

  • ’contam_detection_map’: 2D array with number of detected contaminating lines per pixel

  • ’wavelength’: 1D wavelength array used for fitting

  • ’header’: FITS header from the original cube

  • ’wave_range’: (wavelength_min, wavelength_max) actually used for the fit

  • ’flux_unit’: unit of ‘flux_map’/’contam_flux_map’

Return type:

dict

Raises:

  • RuntimeError – if the CO line list for the cube’s wavelength range cannot be fetched from HITRAN

  • ValueError – if cube_data has no cube loaded

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> flux_map_result = create_flux_map(cube, n_jobs=4)
>>> print(f"Map shape: {flux_map_result['flux_map'].shape}, unit: {flux_map_result['flux_unit']}")
cube_explorer.api.save_flux_map(result, out_path, species=None, cube_data=None)[source]

Save a Flux Map result to a FITS file. This is the Export button of the Flux Map window. The first image is the flux map. The extensions hold the detection counts and the contaminating lines.

Parameters:

  • result (dict) – Result of create_flux_map()

  • out_path (str) – Path of the FITS file to write

  • species (str, optional) – Species of the target lines, for example ‘CO’. None writes ‘Target’.

  • cube_data (CubeData, optional) – Loaded cube. It gives the instrument name if the header has none.

Returns:

None

Example

>>> flux = create_flux_map(cube, target_catalog_path="co_lines.ecsv")
>>> save_flux_map(flux, "co_flux_map.fits", species="CO", cube_data=cube)

Rotational Diagram

cube_explorer.api.rotational_diagram(fluxes, flux_errors, molecular_data=None, OPR=None, fit_opr=False, opr_grid=None, fit1T=True, fit2T=False, R=None, dist=140, upper_limits=None, progress_callback=None, molecule='H2', isotopologue=1)[source]

Fit a rotational diagram (1T and/or 2T) to a set of line fluxes. Dispatches to the H2-specific fitter (hardcoded partition function, OPR support) or the general HITRAN-based fitter (any molecule, e.g. CO) depending on molecule. R is optional. Without R, N is a total molecule count instead of a column density.

Parameters:

  • fluxes (dict) – {J: flux_value}, J is the upper rotational level

  • flux_errors (dict) – {J: flux_error}

  • molecular_data (dict) – ‘wavelengths’, ‘Aul’, ‘Eu’, ‘gu’ keys, each {J: value}

  • OPR (float) – Fixed ortho-para ratio (H2 only; ignored otherwise)

  • fit_opr (bool) – Grid-search OPR to minimize chi-squared (H2 only; ignored otherwise)

  • opr_grid (array) – OPR values to search (H2 only). Defaults to np.linspace(0.1, 5.0, 200)

  • fit1T (bool) – Report the 1T fit (always computed regardless, as 2T’s own seed)

  • fit2T (bool) – Perform the 2T fit

  • R (float) – Emitting radius (AU), or None

  • dist (float) – Distance (pc)

  • upper_limits (dict) – {J: True} for measurements marked as upper limits

  • progress_callback (callable) – (phase, current, total) -> None, for a GUI progress bar

  • molecule (str) – Species being fit, per get_available_molecules()

  • isotopologue (int) – HITRAN isotopologue number for molecule (ignored for H2)

Returns:

Fit results. “OPR”/”OPR_err”/”OPR_err_pos”/”OPR_err_neg” keys

are present only when molecule == ‘H2’

Return type:

results (dict)

Raises:

ValueError – if neither fit1T nor fit2T is True

cube_explorer.api.save_rotational_fit(path, results, header_text=None)[source]

Save a rotational-diagram fit to a CSV file: one row for each point of the diagram, then the fit line. This is Save Fit in the rotational-diagram window. The lines that start with “#” at the top hold the results.

Parameters:

  • path (str) – Path of the CSV file to write

  • results (dict) – The ‘results’ of fit_region or fit_pixel, or the result of rotational_diagram. It must have ‘_plot_data’.

  • header_text (str, optional) – Text for the “#” lines at the top. None writes the single numbers of the ‘1T’ and ‘2T’ entries.

Returns:

None

Raises:

ValueError – if results has no ‘_plot_data’

Example

>>> fit = fit_region(cube, lines)
>>> save_rotational_fit("fit.csv", fit['results'])
cube_explorer.api.save_line_fluxes(path, lines)[source]

Save the line fluxes to a CSV file with the columns species, wavelength, flux, flux_error and upper_limit. This is Save Fluxes in the rotational-diagram window. Read it with load_line_fluxes. A line with no flux is not written.

Parameters:

  • path (str) – Path of the CSV file to write

  • lines (list) – One dict for each line, with ‘species’, ‘wavelength’ (um), ‘flux’ and ‘flux_error’ (erg/s/cm2). A line with ‘upper_limit’ True is written as an upper limit.

Returns:

Number of lines written

Return type:

int

Raises:

ValueError – if no line has a flux

cube_explorer.api.load_line_fluxes(path)[source]

Read a CSV file of lines and add the HITRAN constants that the rotational diagram needs. This is Import from CSV in the rotational-diagram window. The file needs the columns species and wavelength (um). The columns flux, an error column and upper_limit are optional. Each line is matched to the nearest HITRAN line. A line with no match is flagged (‘hitran_matched’ False) and has no A, E_u and g_u.

Parameters:

path (str) – Path of the CSV file

Returns:

One dict for each valid row. It is the line_table of fit_region and create_rotational_diagram_map. A row with flux and flux_error also gives the fluxes for rotational_diagram.

Return type:

list

Raises:

ValueError – if the file is empty, has no species or wavelength column, or has no valid row

Example

>>> lines = load_line_fluxes("H2_lines.csv")
>>> result = fit_region(cube, lines)

Rotational Diagram Maps

These functions fit the rotational diagram at the pixels of one cube, or of several cubes with different pixel scales (the _multi versions). The user guide page Rotational Diagram has worked examples.

Fits of one cube:

cube_explorer.api.fit_region(cube_data, line_table, mask=None, molecule='H2', isotopologue=1, opr=None, fit_opr=False, opr_grid=None, dist_pc=140.0, r_au=None, min_lines=3, dedup_tol_um=1e-05, contam_lines=None, fit2t=False)[source]

Fit one rotational diagram to a cube’s summed spectrum over a region. This is the same fit the GUI’s Run Fit button runs. Pass a mask to sum only some pixels, or omit it to sum the whole cube.

Parameters:

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube from load_cube()

  • line_table (list) – Line dicts with ‘wavelength’, ‘a_coeff’, ‘e_upper’, ‘Gp’, and ‘branch’/’j_lower’ for H2 S-branch lines – the same rows the GUI’s HITRAN fetch or CSV import populate

  • mask (np.ndarray, optional) – 2D boolean array, same spatial shape as the cube. True pixels are summed; None sums every pixel

  • molecule (str) – Species name; ‘H2’ uses the OPR-capable fitter

  • isotopologue (int) – HITRAN isotopologue number, ignored for H2

  • opr (float, optional) – Fixed ortho-para ratio, H2 only

  • fit_opr (bool) – Grid-search OPR to minimize chi-squared, H2 only

  • opr_grid (array, optional) – OPR values to search, H2 only

  • dist_pc (float) – Source distance in parsecs

  • r_au (float, optional) – Emitting region radius in AU. None reports Ncol as a total molecule count instead of a column density

  • min_lines (int) – Fewest detected lines needed before fitting

  • dedup_tol_um (float) – Co-located-line merge tolerance in microns

  • contam_lines (pd.DataFrame, optional) – Contaminating lines to give their own component in the fit, same format create_flux_map accepts

  • fit2t (bool) – Report the two-temperature fit instead of 1T

Returns:

‘status’ (int, one of STATUS_OK/STATUS_NO_DATA/STATUS_TOO_FEW_LINES/

STATUS_FIT_FAILED), ‘n_pixels’, ‘n_lines’, and on STATUS_OK also ‘results’ (rotational_diagram()’s own return value, with a ‘1T’ or ‘2T’ entry depending on fit2t); otherwise ‘reason’ explains why no fit was attempted

Return type:

dict

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> result = fit_region(cube, line_table)
>>> if result['status'] == STATUS_OK:
...     print(result['results']['1T']['T'])
cube_explorer.api.fit_pixel(cube_data, x, y, line_table, molecule='H2', isotopologue=1, opr=None, fit_opr=False, opr_grid=None, dist_pc=140.0, r_au=None, min_lines=3, dedup_tol_um=1e-05, contam_lines=None, n_sigma=3.0, fit2t=False)[source]

Fit one rotational diagram to a single pixel’s own spectrum. This is fit_region for one pixel instead of a summed region.

Parameters:

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube from load_cube()

  • x (int) – Spatial x pixel index

  • y (int) – Spatial y pixel index

  • line_table (list) – Line dicts, see fit_region

  • molecule – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • isotopologue – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • opr – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • fit_opr – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • opr_grid – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • dist_pc – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • r_au – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • min_lines – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • dedup_tol_um – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • contam_lines – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • fit2t – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • n_sigma (float) – Detection threshold in noise sigmas. A line below it is an upper limit and is left out of the fit. 3.0 by default

Returns:

Same shape as fit_region’s return, for this one pixel

Return type:

dict

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> result = fit_pixel(cube, 21, 21, line_table)
cube_explorer.api.create_rotational_diagram_map(cube_data, line_table, molecule='H2', isotopologue=1, opr=None, fit_opr=False, opr_grid=None, dist_pc=140.0, r_au=None, min_lines=3, dedup_tol_um=1e-05, n_jobs=8, contam_lines=None, progress_callback=None, cancel_flag=None, n_sigma=3.0, fit2t=False)[source]

Fit a rotational diagram at every pixel of one cube. Same fit as the GUI’s Run Map button, run once per pixel.

Parameters:

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube from load_cube()

  • line_table (list) – Line dicts, see fit_region

  • molecule – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • isotopologue – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • opr – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • fit_opr – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • opr_grid – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • dist_pc – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • r_au – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • dedup_tol_um – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • contam_lines – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • min_lines (int) – Fewest lines a pixel needs, checked separately at each pixel – one pixel can use different lines than its neighbor. Raise this for fit2t (a 2T fit has 4 free parameters, not 2)

  • n_jobs (int) – Worker threads, one cube row per task

  • progress_callback (callable, optional) – progress_callback(done_pixels, total_pixels)

  • cancel_flag (object, optional) – Object with a .cancelled attribute, checked between rows so a long-running map can be stopped early

  • n_sigma (float) – Detection threshold in noise sigmas, 3.0 by default. A line below it is an upper limit and stays NaN in the maps. Not applied to ‘region_fit’, whose whole-cube sum keeps the 3-sigma rule

  • fit2t (bool) – Report the two-temperature fit instead of 1T, at every pixel

Returns:

‘T’, ‘T_err’ (2D float32, K), ‘Ncol’, ‘Ncol_err’ (2D float64, cm^-2, or molecules if r_au is None) –

component 1 (1T’s only component, or 2T’s T1); ‘T2’, ‘T2_err’, ‘Ncol2’, ‘Ncol2_err’ (2T’s T2 component, all-NaN when fit2t is False); ‘fit2t’, ‘n_lines’ (2D int, lines used per pixel), ‘status’ (2D int, one of STATUS_OK/STATUS_NO_DATA/STATUS_TOO_FEW_LINES/STATUS_FIT_FAILED), ‘region_fit’ (the whole-cube-summed anchor fit, same as fit_region’s return), plus ‘header’, ‘wave_range’, ‘molecule’, ‘dist_pc’, ‘r_au’, ‘opr’, ‘kept_lines’, ‘dropped_lines’

Return type:

dict

Raises:

ValueError – if a multi-cube list is not on one spatial grid

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> result = create_rotational_diagram_map(cube, line_table, n_jobs=4)
>>> print(f"Fitted {(result['status'] == STATUS_OK).sum()} pixels")

Fits of several cubes at different pixel scales:

cube_explorer.api.fit_region_multi(cubes_and_lines, molecule='H2', isotopologue=1, opr=None, fit_opr=False, opr_grid=None, dist_pc=140.0, r_au=None, min_lines=3, dedup_tol_um=1e-05, contam_lines=None, fit2t=False)[source]

Fit one rotational diagram from several cubes at once, one line per cube. This is fit_region for many cubes instead of one. No convolution or reprojection is needed here, since every pixel of every cube is summed.

Parameters:

  • cubes_and_lines (list) – (CubeData, line_dict) pairs, one per input cube

  • molecule – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • isotopologue – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • opr – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • fit_opr – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • opr_grid – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • dist_pc – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • r_au – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • min_lines – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • dedup_tol_um – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • contam_lines – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • fit2t – Same meaning as in fit_region

Returns:

‘status’ (int, one of STATUS_OK/STATUS_TOO_FEW_LINES/STATUS_FIT_FAILED),

’n_lines’, ‘n_pixels’ (total spaxels summed, across every cube), ‘n_cubes’, and on STATUS_OK also ‘results’; otherwise ‘reason’

Return type:

dict

Example

>>> cubes_and_lines = [(load_cube("h2_s1.fits"), {"wavelength": 17.034846}),
...                    (load_cube("h2_s2.fits"), {"wavelength": 12.278612})]
>>> result = fit_region_multi(cubes_and_lines)
cube_explorer.api.fit_pixel_multi(result, x, y, molecule='H2', isotopologue=1, opr=None, fit_opr=False, opr_grid=None, dist_pc=140.0, r_au=None, min_lines=3, fit2t=False)[source]

Re-fit one pixel of a create_rotational_diagram_map_multi result. Uses its cached per-line maps instead of redoing the convolution.

Parameters:

  • result (dict) – Output of create_rotational_diagram_map_multi

  • x (int) – Spatial x index on the result’s common grid

  • y (int) – Spatial y index on the result’s common grid

  • molecule – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • isotopologue – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • opr – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • fit_opr – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • opr_grid – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • dist_pc – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • r_au – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • min_lines – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • fit2t – Same meaning as in fit_region

Returns:

Same shape as fit_pixel’s return, for this pixel of the common grid

Return type:

dict

Raises:

KeyError – if result has no cached per-line maps (predates this function, or came from a different map type)

Example

>>> result = create_rotational_diagram_map_multi(cubes_and_lines)
>>> refit = fit_pixel_multi(result, 10, 15, fit_opr=True)
cube_explorer.api.create_rotational_diagram_map_multi(cubes_and_lines, molecule='H2', isotopologue=1, opr=None, fit_opr=False, opr_grid=None, dist_pc=140.0, r_au=None, min_lines=3, dedup_tol_um=1e-05, n_jobs=8, contam_lines=None, progress_callback=None, cancel_flag=None, n_sigma=3.0, fit2t=False)[source]

Fit a rotational diagram at every pixel of a common grid built from several cubes at different pixel scales, one line per cube. Convolves and reprojects each cube onto that grid first, then fits like Run Map.

Parameters:

  • cubes_and_lines (list) – (CubeData, line_dict) pairs, one per input cube, at least 2

  • molecule – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • isotopologue – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • opr – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • fit_opr – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • opr_grid – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • dist_pc – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • r_au – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • min_lines – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • dedup_tol_um – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • contam_lines – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • fit2t – Same meaning as in fit_region

  • n_jobs (int) – Worker threads for each cube’s native-grid extraction

  • progress_callback (callable, optional) – progress_callback(done_units, total_units), spanning every native-grid extraction plus the final per-pixel fit

  • cancel_flag (object, optional) – Object with a .cancelled attribute

  • n_sigma (float) – Detection threshold in noise sigmas, 3.0 by default. Applies to the native fits only; the convolved maps get no second test. Not applied to ‘region_fit’, whose whole-cube sum keeps the 3-sigma rule

Returns:

‘T’, ‘T_err’ (2D float32, K), ‘Ncol’, ‘Ncol_err’ (2D float64, cm^-2, or molecules if r_au is None) –

component 1; ‘T2’, ‘T2_err’, ‘Ncol2’, ‘Ncol2_err’ (2T’s T2 component, all-NaN when fit2t is False); ‘fit2t’, ‘n_lines’ (2D int), ‘status’ (2D int, see create_rotational_diagram_map), ‘region_fit’ (the whole-cube- summed anchor fit, same as fit_region_multi’s return), plus ‘dst_wcs’ (the new common-grid WCS), ‘molecule’, ‘dist_pc’, ‘r_au’, ‘opr’, ‘min_lines’, ‘t_cap’, ‘worst_pix_arcsec’, ‘kept_lines’, ‘dropped_lines’

Return type:

dict

Raises:

ValueError – if fewer than 2 pairs are given, a cube has no readable celestial WCS/pixel scale, or two inputs share no sky coverage

Example

>>> cubes_and_lines = [(load_cube("h2_s1.fits"), {"wavelength": 17.034846}),
...                    (load_cube("h2_s2.fits"), {"wavelength": 12.278612})]
>>> result = create_rotational_diagram_map_multi(cubes_and_lines, n_jobs=4)
>>> print(f"Common grid: {result['T'].shape}, worst pixel scale: "
...       f"{result['worst_pix_arcsec']:.4f} arcsec")

The steps of Run Map, one at a time. These are the “Calculate Maps”, “Convolve Maps”, and “Run Map” buttons of the rotational diagram window:

cube_explorer.api.compute_native_line_maps(cubes_and_lines, contam_lines=None, n_jobs=8, dedup_tol_um=1e-05, progress_callback=None, cancel_flag=None, region_masks=None, n_sigma=3.0)[source]

Fit each line at the native resolution of its own cube. This is the Calculate Maps button of the rotational-diagram window, and the first step of Run Map. The next step is convolve_line_maps. Scripts that call this need an if __name__ == "__main__": guard on Windows/macOS.

Parameters:

  • cubes_and_lines (list) – (CubeData, line_dict) pairs, one per input cube

  • contam_lines (pandas.DataFrame, optional) – Contaminating lines, or None

  • n_jobs (int) – Number of worker processes for each cube

  • dedup_tol_um (float) – Co-located-line merge tolerance in microns

  • progress_callback (callable, optional) – progress_callback(done_pixels, total_pixels)

  • cancel_flag (object, optional) – Object with a .cancelled attribute

  • region_masks (dict, optional) – {CubeData: 2D boolean mask}. Only the pixels in the mask are fitted for that cube. A cube that is not in the dict is fitted at every pixel.

  • n_sigma (float) – Detection threshold in noise sigmas (default 3.0). This is the only step that applies a threshold. The later steps use the maps as they are.

Returns:

‘kept_lines’, ‘dropped_lines’, ‘native_flux_maps’, ‘native_flux_error_maps’, ‘native_fit_flux_maps’, ‘native_status_maps’, ‘native_ul_ceiling_maps’ (lists of 2D arrays, one for each kept line), ‘native_wcs’, ‘native_headers’, ‘native_shapes’, ‘native_pix_arcsec’, ‘native_instrument’ and ‘cube_filenames’. Pass it to convolution_plan, convolve_line_maps or save_line_maps.

Return type:

dict

Raises:

ValueError – if no pair is given, a cube has no celestial WCS or pixel scale, or two cubes share no sky coverage

Example

>>> native = compute_native_line_maps([(load_cube("s1.fits"), {"wavelength": 17.0348, ...}),
...                                    (load_cube("s2.fits"), {"wavelength": 12.2786, ...})])
>>> save_line_maps(native, "native_maps")
cube_explorer.api.convolution_plan(native_result)[source]

Show what convolve_line_maps will do, without doing it. This is the table that the GUI shows before Convolve Maps and Run Map. The line with the longest wavelength is the reference.

Parameters:

native_result (dict) – Result of compute_native_line_maps

Returns:

‘worst_pix_arcsec’ (pixel scale of the reference line), ‘dst_shape’ (shape of the output grid), ‘per_cube’ (one dict for each line: ‘wavelength’, ‘instrument’, ‘filename’, ‘native_pix_arcsec’, ‘sigma_arcsec’, ‘sigma_pix’) and ‘dropped_lines’

Return type:

dict

Raises:

ValueError – if a line is from an instrument that has no PSF formula (only MIRI and NIRSpec have one)

cube_explorer.api.convolve_line_maps(native_result)[source]

Convolve every native line map to the resolution of the line with the longest wavelength, and reproject it onto the grid of that line. This is the Convolve Maps button of the rotational-diagram window, and the second step of Run Map. The error maps go through the same steps.

Parameters:

native_result (dict) – Result of compute_native_line_maps (or of merge of imported maps, see create_rotational_diagram_map_mixed)

Returns:

‘kept_lines’, ‘line_flux_maps’, ‘line_flux_error_maps’ (the convolved maps, all on one grid), ‘dst_wcs’, ‘dst_shape’, ‘worst_pix_arcsec’, ‘reference_wavelength’, and the native maps that went in. Pass it to combine_line_maps or save_line_maps.

Return type:

dict

Raises:

ValueError – if a line is from an instrument that has no PSF formula (only MIRI and NIRSpec have one)

Example

>>> convolved = convolve_line_maps(native)
>>> save_line_maps(convolved, "convolved_maps.zip")
cube_explorer.api.combine_line_maps(convolved_result, molecule='H2', isotopologue=1, opr=None, fit_opr=False, opr_grid=None, dist_pc=140.0, r_au=None, min_lines=3, region_fit=None, progress_callback=None, cancel_flag=None, fit2t=False)[source]

Fit a rotational diagram at every pixel of the convolved line maps. This is the last step of Run Map. It has no detection threshold of its own. The threshold was set in compute_native_line_maps.

Parameters:

  • convolved_result (dict) – Result of convolve_line_maps

  • molecule (str) – Species name. ‘H2’ uses the fitter with the ortho-para ratio.

  • isotopologue (int) – HITRAN isotopologue number, not used for H2

  • opr (float, optional) – Fixed ortho-para ratio, H2 only

  • fit_opr (bool) – Search the ortho-para ratio at every pixel, H2 only

  • opr_grid (array, optional) – Ratios to search, H2 only

  • dist_pc (float) – Distance in parsecs

  • r_au (float, optional) – Emitting radius in AU. A map does not use the value: with a radius, N is per cm^2 of the area of each pixel. None gives molecules per pixel.

  • min_lines (int) – Fewest detected lines that a pixel needs for a fit

  • region_fit (dict, optional) – Result of fit_region_multi, to add the fit of the summed region

  • progress_callback (callable, optional) – progress_callback(done_pixels, total_pixels)

  • cancel_flag (object, optional) – Object with a .cancelled attribute

  • fit2t (bool) – Report the two-temperature fit instead of the one-temperature fit

Returns:

The same as create_rotational_diagram_map_multi: ‘T’, ‘T_err’, ‘Ncol’, ‘Ncol_err’, ‘T2’, ‘T2_err’, ‘Ncol2’, ‘Ncol2_err’, ‘n_lines’, ‘status’, ‘dst_wcs’ and more. Save it with save_rotational_diagram_map_fits.

Return type:

dict

Lines from flux maps that were made before (the “Load Maps” button), and runs that mix them with lines from cubes:

cube_explorer.api.import_line_map(fits_path, species=None, wavelength=None, error_pct=None)[source]

Read a flux map that was made before, for example by Export of the Gaussian map, as one line of a rotational diagram. This is the Load Maps (Import Map) button. The line has no cube. Its map goes straight into create_rotational_diagram_map_mixed.

The species and the wavelength come from the FITS header (the MOLECULE and LINEWAVE keywords) when it has them. A value that you give replaces the header value. The Einstein A, the upper energy and the statistical weight come from the header, or from the HITRAN line nearest to the wavelength.

Parameters:

  • fits_path (str) – Path of the FITS file of the flux map

  • species (str, optional) – Species, for example ‘H2’. Needed if the header has no MOLECULE keyword.

  • wavelength (float, optional) – Line wavelength in um. Needed if the header has no LINEWAVE keyword.

  • error_pct (float, optional) – Flat error in percent of the flux. Needed if the file has no error map (an ERR extension). It is not used if the file has one.

Returns:

A line dict with ‘wavelength’, ‘species’, ‘transition’, ‘hitran_matched’ and ‘imported_map’ (the map, its error, its WCS and its pixel scale). If HITRAN has no match, ‘hitran_matched’ is False and the line has no A, E_u or g_u, so it is not fitted until you add them.

Return type:

dict

Raises:

ValueError – if the species, the wavelength or the error percent is needed and not given, or the file has no 2D image with a celestial WCS

Example

>>> line = import_line_map("s1_gaussian_area_map.fits", error_pct=20.0)
>>> result = create_rotational_diagram_map_mixed([(cube, other_line)], [line])
cube_explorer.api.fit_region_mixed(cubes_and_lines, imported_lines, molecule='H2', isotopologue=1, opr=None, fit_opr=False, opr_grid=None, dist_pc=140.0, r_au=None, min_lines=3, dedup_tol_um=1e-05, contam_lines=None, region_masks=None, imported_region_masks=None, fit2t=False)[source]

  • min_lines – The same as in fit_region_multi

Saving the maps:

cube_explorer.api.save_line_maps(result, output_path, molecule=None)[source]

Save the flux map of every line of a rotational-diagram result. This is the Save Maps button of the rotational-diagram window, without the PNG files. The native maps go in ‘Flux Maps/fits’ and the convolved maps in ‘Convolved Maps/fits’. Each file is <species>_<flux or convolved>_<wavelength>um.fits.

Parameters:

  • result (dict) – Result of compute_native_line_maps (native maps), convolve_line_maps (convolved maps), create_rotational_diagram_map (native maps) or create_rotational_diagram_map_multi (both)

  • output_path (str) – A folder, or a path that ends in .zip to write one zip file

  • molecule (str, optional) – Species name for the file names and headers. None uses the one in the result, or ‘H2’.

Returns:

{‘Flux Maps’: number of native maps written, ‘Convolved Maps’: number of convolved maps written}. A group that the result does not have is not in the dict.

Return type:

dict

Raises:

ValueError – if the result has no line maps

Example

>>> native = compute_native_line_maps(cubes_and_lines)
>>> convolved = convolve_line_maps(native)
>>> save_line_maps(convolved, "convolved_maps.zip")
cube_explorer.api.save_rotational_diagram_map_fits(result, output_path)[source]

Write a rotational-diagram-map result to a multi-extension FITS file: one image HDU each for T, T_err, Ncol, Ncol_err, n_lines, and status – plus T2/T2_err/Ncol2/Ncol2_err when the result is a 2T fit.

Parameters:

  • result (dict) – Output of create_rotational_diagram_map or create_rotational_diagram_map_multi

  • output_path (str) – Destination FITS path

Returns:

None

Example

>>> result = create_rotational_diagram_map(cube, line_table)
>>> save_rotational_diagram_map_fits(result, "rot_diag_map.fits")

The outcome of each fit is one of these values:

  • STATUS_OK

  • STATUS_NO_DATA

  • STATUS_TOO_FEW_LINES

  • STATUS_FIT_FAILED

Helpers

cube_explorer.api.fetch_hitran_lines(lam_min, lam_max, molecule, isotopologue=1, refresh_cache=False, v_upper=None, v_lower=None)[source]

Get the lines of one molecule from HITRAN, or from the local copy when there is one. This is Fetch HITRAN in the GUI. Each line is a dict with ‘wavelength’ (um, vacuum), ‘a_coeff’, ‘e_upper’, ‘Gp’, ‘transition’ and more.

Parameters:

  • lam_min (float) – Start of the wavelength range in um

  • lam_max (float) – End of the wavelength range in um

  • molecule (str) – Molecule name, for example ‘H2’ or ‘CO’

  • isotopologue (int) – HITRAN isotopologue number (default 1). None gives all of them.

  • refresh_cache (bool) – True fetches the lines again, even if a copy is stored

  • v_upper (int, optional) – Keep only lines with this upper vibrational level

  • v_lower (int, optional) – Keep only lines with this lower vibrational level

Returns:

The line dicts, sorted by wavelength. Empty if HITRAN has no line in the range.

Return type:

list

Raises:

RuntimeError – if the lines could not be fetched (for example, no network and no local copy)

Example

>>> lines = fetch_hitran_lines(4.6, 5.3, 'CO', v_upper=1, v_lower=0)
cube_explorer.api.doppler_shift_factor(velocity)[source]

Give the number that moves observed wavelengths to rest wavelengths for a systemic velocity. This is the multiplicative Doppler shift of the GUI: rest = observed / (1 + v/c).

Parameters:

velocity (float) – Systemic velocity in km/s. Positive means moving away (redshift).

Returns:

The factor. Multiply the wavelengths by it.

Return type:

float

Example

>>> rest_wavelength = cube.wavelength * doppler_shift_factor(17.5)
